agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (lead) / European Space Agency (Huygens probe) / Agenzia Spaziale Italiana (high-gain antenna + radar)
payload: Saturn orbiter (~5712 kg dry) + Huygens descent probe (~318 kg, ESA-built, landed on Titan 2005-01-14)
credit: © NASA / JPL-Caltech / ESA / ASI / Space Science Institute — joint U.S. / European public-domain mission. Cassini orbited Saturn for 13 years (2004-2017), completing 294 orbits and 162 close moon flybys. Highlights: Huygens landed on Titan 2005-01-14 (first soft landing in the outer solar system); discovered Enceladus's plumes 2005 (~100 geysers from the south-polar tiger stripes); resolved Saturn's hexagonal polar storm; mapped Titan's lake system via radar; first observation of seasonal change on Saturn (Cassini covered nearly half a Saturnian year). Grand Finale (2017-04-23 to 2017-09-15) — 22 ring-gap orbits + atmospheric entry that destroyed the spacecraft over Saturn's cloud tops, ending the mission for planetary-protection reasons (preventing future biological contamination of Enceladus or Titan).
